probeLean:
import JevHammerBenchmark.BayesStudy
import Mathlib
open Lean Meta Elab Command JevHammerBenchmark
set_option maxHeartbeats 0
run_cmd liftTermElabM do
  let _ : MonadExceptOf Exception MetaM :=
    { (inferInstance : MonadExceptOf Exception MetaM) with tryCatch := tryCatchRuntimeEx }
  let mode := (← IO.getEnv "WARMUP_PROBE").getD "independent"
  let method := BayesStudy.bayesStructuralTarget
  let before ← IO.getNumHeartbeats
  let start ← IO.monoMsNow
  if mode == "legacy" then
    let failed ← try
      JevHammer.withHeartbeatBudget 200000 do
        discard <| method.validate #[]
        method.warmup
      pure false
    catch e =>
      let msg ← e.toMessageData.toString
      unless msg.contains "heartbeats" do throw e
      IO.println s!"Expected legacy cold-start failure: {msg}"
      pure true
    unless failed do throwError "legacy cold start unexpectedly passed; diagnosis not reproduced"
  else
    discard <| JevHammer.withHeartbeatBudget 200000 <| method.runWarmup #[]
  IO.println s!"{mode}: elapsedMs={(← IO.monoMsNow) - start}, heartbeats={(← IO.getNumHeartbeats) - before}"
reproduction: Write probeLean to a temporary .lean file and set JEVSELECTOR_PUBLIC_INDEX and JEVSELECTOR_BAYES to the artifacts from the Bayes protocol.
Run WARMUP_PROBE=legacy lake env lean <file> in a fresh process; it must catch the original 200000-heartbeat initialization timeout.
Run WARMUP_PROBE=independent lake env lean <file> in another fresh process; it must complete.
Keep both processes serial in one bounded 16 GB, zero-swap job. No Jev API key or neural service is required.
